questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: To take a break from navigating both 15 h/week student job and full time studies at the same time.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Being closer to nature

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, I felt very well informed from both University of Copenhagen and the University of Bern

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A welcome week organised by the University of Bern

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Easy to find through
studentlodge.ch
but not recommendable. I would recommend looking after a shared flat (called WG) e.g. through
https://www.wgzimmer.ch/home.html

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Try and search for other possibilities than the studentlodge and avoid a fixed contract

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There are fine guidelines to figure out the different systems. You can also drop classes after semester start which was a bit confusing to me

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Documents and introduction in the welcome week

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful if I signed up early enough

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Courses change from semester to semester but try and stay updated a few months before and make sure you sign up when the registration period opens so you get a spot on your wanted courses

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I learned a lot from some courses and others not so much. All courses are quite small in credits which gave me a feeling of not going so much in depth as Im used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had many coursed that required more active participation which I practised a lot, that was nice (seminars). I also felt closer to the professors there than I do at UCPH because the classrooms where quite small and I had the same professors in mulitple courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Philosophical foundations of climate change policy and economics
Philosophical issues when modelling climate change

Engaged professors and critical views on the climate science disciplines. I learned a lot from them - another perspective on the climate science philosophy of science. I also recommend taking a german language course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: A problem with moths in my studentlodge so I had to buy sealed containers

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most things are generally more expensive than in Denmark. A pita in town is double the price as in Copenhagen. The train is also expensive but helps with the halffare subscription that I recommend to buy on the first day. University sports are (mostly) for free!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very good university sports with a large variety of sports available even for free. You can also take courses in for example skitouring and alpinism for a fair price compared to other places.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Besides Unisport my education arranged their own social activities for everyone affiliated with the programme. That was a really nice and inclusive community who welcomed me a lot. We even went on a weekend in the mountains for all who studied Climate science.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Take a mountain course at unisport and learn something you can't do in Denmark

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the mountains, Berner Oberland is a perfect spot and not far away with the train. In the summer, go floating with a drybag in the river through town like all the locals and eat ice cream from Gelateria di Berna.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was alright, they are a little strict in Switzerland and reserved but I think Danes have a similar reputation

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be openminded and participate in student organised events for your programme. I got a lot of swiss friends at the end so it is definitely possible

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That they were not as experienced with groupwork and generally did not like to be to direct in communication, where I come from a more 'lets talk about expectations out loud'. I also think the different approaches to AI was a little challenging but I think that's less about Bern and more about our time.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They were relaxed, not too busy and not stressed about the future or study performances from what I experienced. Less competitive study environment than what I've experienced in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Take advantage of the magnificent nature
Engage with the language(s) if you can
Try a whole new sport at Unisport

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try and think about the exam dates for your courses cause they can overlap and you will have quite a few different smaller courses at the end

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being in a more relaxed study environment without a job on the side so I could spend my freetime in the mountains

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That my landlord invented new rules for visitors while I lived at the studentlodge (which is why I dont recommend), which was very stressfull. Luckily, there was a public office in town where you can get a lawyer to help you for free and after that my landlord stepped back a bit.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
